body.statement:
Definition~3.2 of Ejaz and Bareinboim imposes the \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor
restrictions: no ground endogenous variable has an exogenous relational
parent, while a non-relational exogenous parent may be shared only by
attributes of the same instance.  Separately, the completeness and neural
identification statements are made on the intersection with the Section~5
domain satisfying assumptions~(I)--(III), which include finite observed
domains and one global uniform bound on relational-parent multiset size over
every skeleton in the declared domain.  On that intersection, Theorem~5.2
gives the complete identification procedure and Appendix~D,
Corollary~D.7 gives the version-two neural identification correctness result.
body.justification: The comparator qualification relies on the source's separate Definition~3.2 anchor and Section~5 domain statements.
body.gap: This is cited substrate; it does not enlarge the structural class for which the present interval is sharp.
body.consumer: The one-row theorem uses this node to delimit exactly where completeness and neural correctness may be invoked.
